Incorporating the July 2021 SLOOS into the assessment of the July 28, 2021 FOMC statement modestly improves the outlook. The FOMC’s dovish stance (policy rate at 0–0.25%, ongoing asset purchases, tolerance for inflation moderately above 2%) already points to easy financial conditions. The SLOOS corroborates and amplifies this by showing:
- Stronger demand for C&I loans across large, middle-market, and small firms, alongside higher borrower inquiries; banks eased C&I terms, and foreign banks also reported stronger C&I demand tied to inventory, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A.
- Broad easing in consumer credit standards (credit cards, auto, other consumer), with multiple residential mortgage categories easing and multifamily CRE standards easing; QM mortgage demand was stronger. Some caution persists (GSE-eligible mortgage standards unchanged; few subprime originations).

These credit-supply and demand improvements reinforce the FOMC’s message that the flow of credit is supportive, partially offsetting the Financial Stability Report’s cautions about elevated valuations and nonbank vulnerabilities. Net effect: tilt sentiment more positive than the prior FOMC+FSR-only read.
